summary: Delayed token drain and connection reset observed for requests with deep context + high max_tokens
description: Customer ScribeAI reports reproducible request failures for generation calls that combine deep conversation history (~12k tokens) and a large max_tokens setting (>=10k). Calls either hang for >90s and then terminate with a client connection reset or return a 504/502 originating from the finalizer step. Occurs intermittently but with high frequency during sustained bursts.
impact: Several production endpoints for ScribeAI's transcription summarization feature are returning failed completions or hard disconnects during peak traffic. Customer reports user-visible errors and increased retry traffic. This affects a dedicated fleet and is causing increased support load and potential SLA breaches.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Use customer's dedicated API key in prod (us-east).
2) Construct a prompt by concatenating ~12k tokens of conversation history followed by system and user instructions (~2k tokens).
3) Issue a /v1/generate request pinned to redwood/longform-16k with max_tokens set to 10000 and stream=false.
4) Observe request latency: initial tokens stream for ~60-90s then connection resets or the response returns HTTP 504 with finalizer stack trace in logs.
5) Repeat under moderate burst concurrency (10-20 concurrent requests) to reproduce higher failure rate.

investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: KV cache thrashing during deep-context workloads leads to repeated reloads and increased finalizer latency, causing request body write stalls and client resets.
Observed elevated KV eviction rates on srv-77 at time of failures. Evictions correlate with queue growth in finalizer and drain subsystems.
Reproduced locally with a dedicated dev cluster by forcing cache size to 60% of working set; saw identical finalizer backlog and eventual connection resets.
CPU/GPU utilization on involved instances remained moderate (<60%), but I/O spikes (disk and inter-instance RPC) coincided with evictions.
Scheduler logs show delayed task preemption and multiple kernel swaps on busy hosts during bursts, increasing per-token latency.
Client-side timeouts vary by SDK; customers using our SDK with default 90s read timeout hit hard disconnects, while streaming clients sometimes receive partial tokens then stall.
resolution_notes: Mitigation applied (2026-03-11 02:00 UTC): increased KV cache size on affected dedicated pool and tuned eviction policy to favor prefix retention for pinned models.
Rolled out a short-term scheduler throttle to reduce concurrent long-context allocations on the same host to avoid kernel swap thrash.
Added a targeted fallback policy: for requests with context >10k tokens, route to a lower-concurrency node pool with larger cache and higher memory reservations.
Customer instructed to set client-side streaming with keepalive and to add a smaller max_tokens as a short-term workaround (<=6k) to avoid the finalizer-heavy path.
Follow-ups: implement smarter prefetching for KV pages on large-prefix paths, and add metrics to surface finalizer queue length per model + per-instance. Assigned to runtime team (ENG-serve-187).
